citation.author: Elpidorou, Andreas and Freeman, Lauren
citation.title: Fear, Anxiety, and Boredom
citation.in: Szanto, T. and Landweer, H. (eds.), The Routledge Handbook of Phenomenology of Emotions (Routledge, New York)
citation.pages: 1-16 (manuscript/pre-print pagination as extracted; final published pagination may differ)

discipline: philosophy (phenomenology of affectivity) — Heidegger and Sartre in comparative exposition
thesis: Affectivity is constitutive of, not incidental to, human existence. Heidegger's fear, anxiety, and profound boredom form a graded series in which fear is an inauthentic quasi-mood while anxiety and profound boredom are true Grundstimmungen that individuate Dasein toward authenticity; Sartre's emotions are pre-reflective 'magical' transformations of one's relation to the world undertaken when instrumental means fail, a model the authors extend (since Sartre himself never discusses it) to construct a non-pathologizing, potentially functional reading of boredom as perceived-meaninglessness resolved by escape-seeking. The conclusion gestures toward reconciling the two accounts and flags their shared neglect of positive affectivity.
sections: 1 Heidegger and Affectivity (pp.1-7) -- 1.1 Befindlichkeit and Stimmung (pp.2-3); 1.2 Fear, Anxiety, and Boredom (pp.3-7): fear as inauthentic quasi-mood, anxiety as Grundstimmung, the three forms of boredom named with discussion confined to the third

2 Sartre and Affectivity (pp.7-12) -- 2.1 Emotions as Lived Transformations (pp.7-9): the Sketch's magical theory of emotion; 2.2 Fear and Boredom (pp.9-12): Sartre's passive/active fear, then the authors' original Sartrean extension to boredom
3 Conclusion (p.13) -- conciliatory suggestion (Sartrean emotion may presuppose Befindlichkeit) and shared critique of both accounts' neglect of positive affects

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: the entry's one sustained boredom topic; the impersonal 'es ist einem langweilig,' the 'undifferentiated no one,' collapse of the three temporal ekstases, entrancement, and the culminating call-to-action in the Augenblick

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: one defining clause only (FCM sec.19-23), then explicitly bracketed from further discussion

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: one defining clause only (FCM sec.24-28), then explicitly bracketed from further discussion

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: named as an explicit gap (footnote 3); deferred to the authors' own 2015 companion piece rather than developed here

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: becomes central only in the Sartrean half: the 'difficulty' giving rise to boredom is glossed as perceived meaninglessness, lack of interest, or challenge -- an authorial construction, not found in Sartre's own text

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: one sentence, citation-only: inability to maintain attention, alternative goals becoming salient

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: light touch, same sentence as mind-wandering

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: the entry's most consequential boredom claim: boredom can motivate the move 'into a better (i.e., more fulfilling) life,' citing Elpidorou 2018b directly

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: no explicit vocabulary; structural analogue only via the Augenblick/'call to action' as the positive telos profound boredom opens onto

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: absent -- the entry never adopts the state/trait psychological vocabulary used in the authors' own fuller chapter (bor-sec-04)

readings.summary: One-clause definition of becoming-bored-by-something (Gelangweiltwerden von etwas), citing FCM sec.19-23 exactly matching fcm-04's own section range; example given (object, person, state of affairs) but not elaborated.

One-clause definition of being-bored-with-something (Sichlangweilen bei etwas), citing FCM sec.24-28 exactly matching fcm-05's own section range; noted only as a form in which the boring thing is unclear to Dasein, not elaborated.

Primary FCM anchor: the impersonal 'es ist einem langweilig' and 'undifferentiated no one' (FCM 135/203); profound boredom 'no longer permits' passing-the-time (FCM 136/205); entrancement's telling refusal read as itself a 'call for action' issuing in the Augenblick, where Dasein becomes 'the author of its own existential meaning' (FCM 148-152/222-28, FCM 149/224) -- corresponds to fcm-06's own sec.32b.

concepts: Grundstimmung (fundamental mood) vs. Grundbefindlichkeit (fundamental attunement) -- regularized terminologically by the authors, footnoted rather than argued
Augenblick (moment of vision) as call to authentic self-appropriation
passive fear (fainting) vs. active fear (flight) as the same underlying magical negation
boredom as perceived meaninglessness resolved by escape-seeking (the authors' own Sartrean construction)
interlocutors: Martin Heidegger -- Being and Time (Befindlichkeit, Stimmung, fear, anxiety) and The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics (three forms of boredom, primary target for sec.1.2)

Jean-Paul Sartre -- Sketch for a Theory of the Emotions (primary target for sec.2), also Transcendence of the Ego, The Imaginary, Being and Nothingness, Saint Genet, Critique of Dialectical Reason, The Family Idiot (surveyed briefly, p.7-8)
Lauren Freeman (2014) -- 'Toward a Phenomenology of Mood,' cited for the argument that fear is emotion-like rather than mood-like (footnote 7)

Jan Slaby (2014) -- 'The Other Side of Existence: Heidegger on Boredom,' cited as further reading alongside De Beistegui 2003 and the authors' own in-press piece (p.7; NOTE: cited here as 2014, cluster manifest dates bor-sec-13 to 2010 -- likely a working-paper vs. published-book-chapter variant of the same title)
Miguel De Beistegui (2003) -- Thinking with Heidegger: Displacements, cited as further reading on Heidegger and boredom (p.7)
Joseph Fell (1965) and David Weberman (1996) -- cited as critics of Sartre's account of the emotions, specifically its inability to handle positive emotions (p.12)
Matthew Ratcliffe (2008) -- Feelings of Being, cited alongside Elpidorou 2013 and Freeman 2014 as informing empirically-attentive phenomenology of emotion (p.1)
tensions: boredom-as-deficit <-> boredom-as-functional/adaptive -- the entry's own Sartrean reading explicitly 'safeguards one from assuming an overly negative take on boredom' and cites Elpidorou 2018b for boredom's capacity to motivate a 'better... life' (pp.11-12); this entry actively shifts toward the functional pole rather than merely reporting it.

profound boredom is boredom <-> profound boredom is a distinct existential mood -- not adjudicated here; the entry points readers to the authors' own fuller treatment (in press / bor-sec-04) without resolving the question itself (p.7, footnote 9).

pre-reflective/'magical' transformation model of emotion <-> reflective self-report and voluntary counteraction of a felt state -- the entry raises this tension against its own Sartrean account of boredom (checking phones, going for walks as evidence we consciously recognize and fight boredom) without resolving it (p.12).

Heideggerian disclosive/authenticity account of boredom's positive role <-> Sartrean magical/motivational account of boredom's positive role -- both land on a non-pathologizing reading of boredom's third form/functional character but via incompatible theoretical machinery (Grundstimmung-disclosure vs. magical-transformation); the entry's conclusion gestures at reconciling the two frameworks in general (not boredom-specifically) without settling the question (p.13).

negative-affect-centered phenomenology (both philosophers) <-> a needed phenomenology of positive affects (joy, love, awe, hope) -- explicitly named as a shared, unaddressed limitation of both accounts (p.13).
